newsitem.title: CANADA: FOCUS-Canada's Hollinger bids for rest of Southam.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Canada's Hollinger bids for rest of Southam.

text.p: Canadian press baron Conrad Black's Hollinger Inc. offered on Wednesday to buy the rest of its 51 percent-owned newspaper publisher Southam Inc. in a C$923 million ($661 million) cash and stock deal.
Southam shareholders would get C$13.50 ($9.67) a share in cash and a C$10 ($7.17) non-voting special share in Hollinger Canadian, a unit of New York-based Hollinger International Inc.
Toronto-based Southam is Canada's biggest daily newspaper publisher. Its newspapers include the Montreal Gazette, the Ottawa Citizen and Vancouver Sun.

Hollinger Inc. President and Southam Associate Chief Executive David Radler said in a telephone interview that "there are lots of reasons (for taking a subsidiary private) that aren't specific to this company. The main one is you have better access to cash flow."
Some market watchers were unhappy with the C$23.50 ($16.84) a share price, saying it did not reflect the increasingly rosy outlook for Canadian newspaper publishers.
"People would be absolutely nuts to tender to this offer," said Andrew McCreath, a portfolio manager at Toronto brokerage Lawrence & Co.
Southam's four independent directors will form a committee to evaluate the Hollinger offer.
Black's media group gained control of Southam almost a year ago when it bought Power Corp of Canada's 21.5 percent holding, boosting its stake to 41 percent.
Late last year, it bid C$18.75 ($13.44) a share to raise its stake to almost 51 percent, but was forced by the Southam board to raise its offer to C$20 ($14.33).
Radler said Hollinger would not consider raising this bid, saying: "This is our offer."

Southam shares were up C$2.60 to a 52-week high of C$23 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Wednesday after resuming trade following a halt for the Hollinger announcement. Hollinger Inc. was up C5 cents to C$13.15 in Toronto, while Hollinger International was unchanged at $10.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Southam publishes 32 dailies and 58 free and paid circulation newspapers. Hollinger's holdings include several high-profile international papers such as London's Daily Telegraph, the Chicago Sun-Times and Jerusalem Post.
